hollow-legion.title: castellan
names: the Castellan of the Ninth Gate

troubles.name: missing hunters
troubles.text: {leader} of {settlement} says the hunters went out toward {site} a week ago and have not come back.
troubles.solved: The hunters of {settlement} come home from {site}, thin and grateful.
troubles.failed: {settlement} has stopped waiting for its hunters. There will be empty places at their tables this winter.

troubles.name: stolen livestock
troubles.text: Cattle are vanishing from the pastures of {settlement}, and the tracks lead toward {site}.
troubles.solved: The herds of {settlement} graze in peace again now that {site} is quiet.
troubles.failed: {settlement} has lost half its herds. {People} are slaughtering the rest before they too are taken.

troubles.name: trapped miners
troubles.text: A shaft below {settlement} broke into {site}. Something came up, and miners are trapped below.
troubles.solved: The trapped miners of {settlement} climb out into daylight, and the hold sings for a night.
troubles.failed: {settlement} seals the broken shaft with the miners still behind it.

troubles.name: a lost survey team
troubles.text: A survey team from {settlement} went to map the country by {site} and sent no word since.
troubles.solved: The survey team from {settlement} comes home with its maps, and shares them.
troubles.failed: The survey team from {settlement} is given up for lost.

troubles.name: a beast on the move
troubles.text: Something has moved into {site} and hunts the paths of {settlement}. {People} keep their children in at dusk.
troubles.solved: The paths of {settlement} are safe again with {site} cleared.
troubles.failed: {settlement} has given up the paths near {site}. Its people go hungry rather than walk them.

troubles.name: vanishing barges
troubles.text: Barges bound for {settlement} have been vanishing on the water near {site}.
troubles.solved: Barges come down to {settlement} again; whatever took them at {site} is gone.
troubles.failed: No barge will run to {settlement} now. Its quays are empty.

troubles.name: raided pilgrims
troubles.text: Pilgrims on their way to {settlement} are being set upon near {site}.
troubles.solved: Pilgrims walk the road to {settlement} unafraid once {site} is dealt with.
troubles.failed: The pilgrim road to {settlement} is abandoned.

troubles.name: a creature at the spring
troubles.text: Something has taken the spring that waters {settlement}'s fields, out by {site}.
troubles.solved: Water runs to the fields of {settlement} again.
troubles.failed: The fields of {settlement} dry out with the spring still held.

troubles.name: blight in the fields
troubles.text: A grey blight is creeping through the fields of {settlement}. {leader} asks for herbs and coin to burn and replant.
troubles.solved: The fields of {settlement} come back green. They will not forget who paid for the seed.
troubles.failed: The blight takes {settlement}'s harvest. Families pack their carts.

troubles.name: a broken mill
troubles.text: The mill at {settlement} has cracked its wheel. Without timber for a new one, the grain will rot unground.
troubles.solved: The mill at {settlement} turns again on a new wheel, and the miller toasts {town}.
troubles.failed: {settlement}'s mill stands still, and the grain spoils in the sacks.

troubles.name: flooding
troubles.text: Floodwater has risen over the lower houses of {settlement}. They need timber for dikes, and quickly.
troubles.solved: The dikes hold at {settlement}, and the water goes down.
troubles.failed: The flood takes the lower town of {settlement}. Its people come looking for dry ground.

troubles.name: a fever
troubles.text: A fever is going through {settlement}. Their healer asks for draughts, and {leader} for coin to pay for them.
troubles.solved: The fever breaks at {settlement}. Their healer writes to thank {town}.
troubles.failed: The fever burns through {settlement}. Graves are dug at the edge of town.

troubles.name: a cold forge
troubles.text: The great forge of {settlement} has cracked its hearth. Without stone and coin to reline it, their smiths sit idle.
troubles.solved: The forge of {settlement} burns again. Its smiths remember who sent the stone.
troubles.failed: The forge of {settlement} goes cold for good. Its best smiths drift away to find work.

troubles.name: a hard winter
troubles.text: Snow has shut {settlement} in early. Their stores will not last to spring without help.
troubles.solved: {settlement} sees out the winter on {town}'s grain.
troubles.failed: Winter is cruel to {settlement}. Not everyone sees the thaw.

troubles.name: a drought
troubles.text: No rain has fallen on {settlement} for weeks. The wells are low and the crops are burning in the fields.
troubles.solved: {settlement} gets through the dry months on {town}'s grain until the rain comes back.
troubles.failed: The drought empties {settlement}'s granary. Families take to the roads looking for water.

troubles.name: counterfeit coin
troubles.text: False coin is flooding the markets of {settlement}. Their assayer needs ledgers and silver to trace it.
troubles.solved: The coiners of {settlement} are caught, and its merchants trust their scales again.
troubles.failed: No one in {settlement} trusts a coin now. Half its traders have shut their stalls.

band.out: {band} set out for {site} to see to {trouble} themselves.
band.won: {band} come home from {site} with it cleared. {settlement} toasts its own.
band.lost: {band} come back from {site} beaten, {lost} fewer. {leader} sends to {town} for help.
band.taken: {band} come back from {site} beaten. Their captain, {captain}, was taken alive. {leader} begs {town} for help.
band.broken: {band} is no more: too few came back from {site} to call it a band.
band.raised: {settlement} has raised a new band of its own: {band}, under {captain}.
band.rescued: The {party} find {captain} of {band} alive in {site} and bring them home to {settlement}.

projects.name: Mooring tower
projects.text: A tall stone tower with a mooring mast at {settlement}: the town's airship ties up there, unloads fast and sells dear, and its guns keep fliers off.
projects.done: The mooring tower at {settlement} is finished. The airship's first visit draws half the town onto the rooftops.

projects.name: Watchtower
projects.text: A stone tower on the heights above {settlement}, manned by its own people, that sees trouble coming.
projects.done: The watchtower above {settlement} is finished. Its first beacon is lit in {town}'s honour.

projects.name: Bridge
projects.text: A proper bridge on the road to {settlement}: caravans cross in a day what took three.
projects.done: The bridge on the road to {settlement} is open. The first carts across bring a cask for {town}'s council.

projects.name: Caravan patrol
projects.text: Riders who keep the road to {settlement} and see caravans through, paid by {town}.
projects.done: {town}'s riders begin to patrol the road to {settlement}.

projects.name: Waystation
projects.text: Beds, a hearth and a healer for parties on the road: heroes coming back from this country rest there and come home whole.
projects.done: The waystation at {settlement} opens its doors. Its keeper hangs {town}'s banner over the hearth.

projects.name: Great mill
projects.text: A great mill for {settlement}: more grain ground, more to spare, and a better harvest for its allies.
projects.done: The great mill at {settlement} turns for the first time, and the whole village comes to watch.

projects.name: Forge
projects.text: Reline and widen the forges of {settlement}: its smiths work again, and its allies get the best of their work.
projects.done: The forges of {settlement} roar again. Their first blade is sent to {town}.

leader.text: {name} of {settlement} remembers {memory}. A wagon of {good} arrives at the market with their compliments.

hunter.text: {name}, the hunter from {settlement} who remembers {memory}, sends word of what lairs in the country around them.

tracker.text: {name}, the tracker from {settlement} who remembers {memory}, walks in with fresh signs of what moves in the wilds.

surveyor.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, sends copies of the survey maps to {town}.

drover.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, drives a herd to {town}'s market at cost.

miner.text: {name}, the miner from {settlement} who remembers {memory}, sends a load of dressed stone, no charge.

bargeman.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, brings a barge of {good} up to {town} at cost.

pilgrim.text: {name}, the pilgrim from {settlement} who remembers {memory}, prays at {town}'s shrines for its luck.

well-keeper.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, sends the first of the watered harvest to {town}.

farmer.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, sends grain to {town} at cost.

miller.text: {name}, the miller of {settlement} who remembers {memory}, sends flour to {town}'s market at cost.

boatwright.text: {name} of {settlement}, who remembers {memory}, floats a raft of timber down to {town}.

healer.text: {name}, the healer of {settlement} who remembers {memory}, sends draughts for {town}'s heroes.

smith.text: {name}, the smith of {settlement} who remembers {memory}, sends tools to {town} at cost.

reeve.text: {name} of {settlement} remembers {memory}, and sends {good} to {town} with thanks.

assayer.text: {name}, the assayer of {settlement} who remembers {memory}, puts a merchant's debt to {town} in order: {qty} gold.

veteran.text: {name}, once captain of {band}, remembers {memory}. They walk into {town} with their gear on their back: they would fight for it now.

temperaments.name: generous
temperaments.text: open-handed with friends, and quick to share what they have

temperaments.name: shrewd
temperaments.text: a hard bargainer who loves a full caravan more than a friend

temperaments.name: wary
temperaments.text: slow to trust outsiders, slower still to bend to a threat

temperaments.name: proud
temperaments.text: loath to ask anyone for help, and pays well when they must

temperaments.name: devout
temperaments.text: faithful to the shrines, and unwilling to kneel to anything that does not answer prayers

temperaments.name: timid
temperaments.text: anxious to please everyone, the town and its enemies alike

temperaments.name: a puppet
temperaments.text: who rules in an enemy's name

messengers: a merchant up from the south road
reigns.routeNews: The drovers back from {settlement} bring news: {death} {heir}

deaths.age: {old}, their {title}, has died in their sleep at {age}, full of years.
deaths.illness: {old}, their {title}, was taken by a fever at {age}.
deaths.knife: {old}, their {title}, was found dead with a knife in their back. Folk there say the hand was paid by {menace}.
deaths.battle: {old}, their {title}, fell in the fighting when {menace} came down on them.
deaths.broken: {old}, their {title}, rode out with {band} and did not come home.
deaths.overthrown: after hard years their people have had enough of {old} and driven them out.
deaths.puppet: {old}, their {title}, is dead or fled, and {menace} has put its own creature in the seat.
deaths.freed: with {menace}'s shadow gone, the people have thrown down its creature {old}.

reigns.warmer: They think better of {town} than the last did.
reigns.colder: They think less of {town} than the last did.
reigns.puppetHeir: {leader} sits in the seat now, and their tribute goes up the road.

forms.dread: Folk on the road say {settlement} keeps its shutters closed by day now. {People} whisper of {menace} and will not say its name.
forms.tribute: Word comes that {settlement} has begun sending tribute to {menace}. Its carts no longer come to {town}'s market.
forms.cult: Pilgrims say {people} have taken up {menace}'s hymns. There is a new shrine in {settlement}, and nobody will say who it is to.

shadow.lifting: With {source} cleared, the people of {settlements} lift their heads: {menace}'s grip on them loosens.
shadow.lifted: The shadow over {settlement} has lifted. Its people open their shutters and send to {town} again.
shadow.fled: {n} {families} from {settlement} come up the road to {town}, slipping out from under {menace}'s shadow, and pitch tents by the road.
shadow.envoyText: The envoy stays on at {settlement} to remind its people they have friends, and {menace}'s grip on them loosens.
shadow.aidText: {town}'s aid reminds {settlement} it is not alone, and the shadow over it thins.
shadow.rallyOut: {hero} rides out for {settlement} to rally its people against {menace}.
shadow.rallied: {hero} stands in the square at {settlement} and speaks against {menace}. The people take heart, and its shadow over them pales (Persuasion {total} against DC {dc}).
shadow.rallyFailed: {hero} speaks at {settlement}, but the people there are too frightened of {menace} to listen (Persuasion {total} against DC {dc}).
shadow.rallyHurt: On the road home from {settlement}, {menace}'s creatures catch {hero} alone. They limp into town hurt.

relief.text: A relief caravan comes up the road from {settlement}: {food} food for the town under threat, sent by {leader}.
relief.led: A relief caravan comes up the road from {settlement}, led by {contact}, who remembers {memory}: {food} food for the town under threat.
